By Kentaro TsutsumiOctober 29, 2026 at 11:56 PM UTCBookmark

Japan Exchange Group Inc.’s first large-scale reshuffle of the Topix Index goes into effect Friday, part of the biggest overhaul in the benchmark’s history that may shrink the number of constituents by more than one-third.
The weighting of stocks slated for removal in this initial review will be gradually reduced, potentially cutting about 700 names and leaving the index with less than 1,000 members. The revamp also expands index eligibility to market segments geared toward smaller and growth firms, as long as they meet criteria including liquidity. Annual reshuffles will start from October 2028.

Vale SA’s iron ore production fell short of estimates in the third quarter as the world’s largest producer of the steelmaking ingredient faced challenges at a mine in northern Brazil.
Iron ore output totaled 88.35 million metric tons in the three months through September, below the 91.64 million-ton average estimate and down about 6% from a year earlier.

Gold steadied near $4,000 an ounce, and was on track for a second monthly loss, as energy-led inflation raised the prospects for a US rate increase before year-end.
Bullion was little changed after shedding 1.1% in the previous session. The Federal Reserve left the door open for an interest-rate hike before the end of the year to rein in stubborn inflation, and data released Thursday showed a 0.5% rise in the US personal consumption expenditures price index last month. That’s the most since March.

Takeaways by Bloomberg AI
China’s push to internationalize the yuan has entered a “steady, slow, but nonstop” phase that is likely to support further gains in the currency, according to JPMorgan Asset Management.
The yuan may appreciate at least 10% over the long run in real effective exchange-rate terms, Julio Callegari, chief investment officer for Asia fixed income, said in an interview this week. That measure tracks a currency’s strength against a trade-weighted basket of peers while adjusting for inflation.

Rio Tinto Group has suspended underground operations at its massive Oyu Tolgoi copper mine in Mongolia.
A rockfall triggered by a seismic event on Thursday led to three workers being injured, the company said in a statement on Friday. Operations are paused as the company carries out a safety review, it said.

item.title: Fed Is Facing Same Issues Greenspan Did in 2001: Kelton
item.description: Stephanie Kelton, Professor of Public Policy and Economics at Stony Brook University, said the U.S. economy is outperforming its G7 peers, with fiscal support contributing to growth even as the deficit runs at roughly 6.5% of GDP. She noted that about half of the roughly $2 trillion deficit reflects interest costs, and emphasized that higher interest payments become income for bondholders rather than disappearing. She speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close" on October 28th, 2026. (Source: Bloomberg)
